B.explanation: It gives $f = 1.0 \times 10^6 \text{ Hz}$, which is the frequency for a period of $1.0 \text{ } \mu\text{s}$, not $1.0 \text{ ns}$.

Connect period to frequency with $f = 1/T$, which for $10^{-9} \text{ s}$ gives a gigahertz frequency in $\text{Hz}$.

walkthrough: Identify the given period: $T = 1.0 \text{ ns} = 1.0 \times 10^{-9} \text{ s}$.
Use the period-frequency relation $f = 1/T$. Substituting gives $f = 1/(1.0 \times 10^{-9} \text{ s}) = 1.0 \times 10^9 \text{ Hz}$.
Recall all electromagnetic waves travel at $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ in vacuum and obey $c = f\lambda$.
Rearrange for wavelength: $\lambda = c/f = (3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1})/(1.0 \times 10^9 \text{ Hz}) = 0.30 \text{ m}$.
The row with $1.0 \times 10^9 \text{ Hz}$ and $0.30 \text{ m}$ matches the calculation. This is option C
